There are also some foods to avoid when dealing with a bout of diarrhea, and some additional home care tips to consider. Anyone who is experiencing persistent diarrhea should see a doctor, as a person may become dehydrated over time. Diarrhea is a bowel movement that is more liquid than solid or has a loose texture. It is a common problem and may occur a couple of times each year. Diarrhea will usually last no more than 3 days. Soft, bland foods, such as toast, will help to absorb excess water and ease the symptoms of diarrhea. People with chronic digestive conditions, such as irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) or Crohn's disease, may experience diarrhea more regularly. A person's diet is crucial if they are experiencing diarrhea. Some foods might help relieve symptoms of diarrhea while eating other foods can make diarrhea worse.

the self? The poets featured in this volume have written during the last hundred years since World War I into our contemporary experience of conflict. They come primarily from the English-language world but move towards a world literature of global scope. Though writing styles vary greatly, they share an engagement with the task of bearing witness, documenting, and resisting dehumanizing forces that would silence both individual voice and the call for justice. Poetry has the power, as these essays demonstrate, not only to record and interpret violence, but in the very act of writing it, to create its own ethical space in which language, not power, becomes sovereign. Contributors trace the various ways they argue poetry does this work, not only in the public sphere but within the soul of the individual writing it and the communities seeking justice that it informs. The volume offers a compelling map of literary responses to political trauma across the sweep of twentieth and early twenty-first century history. A lifelong cricketer of moderate prowess, he reflects with characteristic wit on his past experiences with the game, which often include spectacular or humbling failures. The recent news about oil spills in China has once again brought attention to the dangers of handling oil sands, even as global demand for these unconventional fuels rises. While oil sands extraction has become more efficient in recent years, it remains an inherently dangerous and destructive process, with concerns about both environmental impact and worker safety. Here are some key points to consider about oil sands handling: What are oil sands? Oil sands, also known as tar sands, are mixtures of sand, clay, water, and bitumen – a thick, heavy, tar-like oil that must be heated to become liquid. They are found abundantly in Canada, Venezuela, and other locations around the world, with Alberta, Canada hosting one of the largest oil sand reserves in the world. Why are oil sands dangerous to handle? Bitumen contains heavy metals and other toxic contaminants that can pose significant health risks, both to workers who handle it directly and to communities living near extraction sites. In fact, Diascia (known as Jacob’s Ladder) is a South African perennial that thrives in partial shade, prefers cool weather and can be maintained for many years in the garden. It's particularly useful as a long-season groundcover where plants such as pansies and primroses cannot survive the summer heat. When you first see Diascia growing in a garden, you may be surprised to learn that it is not a tender annual. In fact, Diascia is surprisingly hardy for a plant from such a warm climate and thrives in coastal gardens. It is also rabbit and deer resistant. Diascia is a small, bushy plant with slender stems and delicate, lacy foliage. The flowers are small and funnel-shaped, and they appear in clusters at the tips of the stems, creating long-lasting, colourful displays. The flowers come in a range of colours, including pink, purple, white and red, and they often have a distinctive veining pattern on the petals.

state Department of Environmental Resources has declared a Level 2 drought emergency for the region, but the town’s reservoirs are hovering near or even above capacity. How can this be? The simple answer is that drought is not just about how much rain you get in a week or month. It is a cumulative process, and we are all feeling the effects of a La Niña-driven drought that began last winter and has continued this entire year. So, while the state is urging us to conserve water – and it remains important to conserve water – the need is not as acute as it would be if the reservoirs were well below capacity. Still, the severity of the drought is undeniable. Lake Winnipesaukee, the state’s largest lake, is at its lowest level on record for this time of year. The lack of snowpack this year means streams and rivers are running low, and the potential for wildfires is heightened. It’s a reminder that the weather in New England is not always predictable,

The error, which was caught by volunteers, could potentially cost presumptive Democratic nominee Hillary Clinton votes in the battleground state and ensure that Republican Donald Trump gets all of Ohio's 18 electoral votes. Franklin County has 1.6 million voters, and Clinton won the county by 2.4 percent.
